title: QR Code Generator
whatIs:
What is QR Code Generator

The QR Code Generator creates Quick Response (QR) codes from any text input using a canvas-based rendering approach. It encodes your input into a QR code matrix following the ISO/IEC 18004 standard, supporting alphanumeric, byte, and kanji encoding modes. The generated QR code uses error correction level M (approximately 15% recovery capacity), which balances readability with data density. The output is rendered directly to an HTML canvas element and can be downloaded as a PNG image.
howToUse:
How to Use QR Code Generator

Step 1: Enter the text, URL, or data you want to encode in the input area.

Step 2: Click Transform. The tool renders a QR code matrix on the canvas.

Step 3: The QR code image appears in the output area. Scan it with any QR reader to verify.

Step 4: Right-click the QR code image to save it as a PNG file, or use the download button if available.
whyUse:
Why Use QR Code Generator

QR codes are ubiquitous for sharing URLs on physical media (posters, business cards, product packaging), enabling contactless payments, linking to WiFi credentials, and creating scannable links for mobile users. Generating them client-side means your encoded data — which may include sensitive URLs or authentication tokens — never touches an external server. This is especially important for WiFi QR codes and payment links.

faq.question: How much data can a QR code hold?
faq.answer: A Version 40 QR code (the largest) can hold up to 4,296 alphanumeric characters, 2,953 bytes, or 1,817 kanji characters. However, smaller versions are faster to scan. For URLs under 200 characters, the generated QR code will be compact and easy to scan.

faq.question: Can I customize the QR code colors?
faq.answer: The generator produces standard black-on-white QR codes for maximum scanning compatibility. Custom colors can reduce scan reliability, especially with low-contrast combinations.

faq.question: What is error correction level M?
faq.answer: Error correction level M means the QR code can recover from approximately 15% damage or obstruction. Higher levels (Q at 25%, H at 30%) allow more recovery but produce denser codes. Level M is the standard balance used by most QR generators.

faq.question: Will this QR code work with all scanners?
faq.answer: Yes. The tool follows the ISO/IEC 18004 standard, and the generated codes use the default byte encoding mode, which is universally supported by all QR code readers, including phone cameras, dedicated scanners, and web-based readers.

title: QR Code Decoder
whatIs:
What is QR Code Decoder

The QR Code Decoder reads and extracts the data encoded in QR code images. It accepts image uploads (PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP) and uses canvas-based image processing to decode the QR code matrix. The decoder works entirely in the browser — the image is drawn to a canvas, pixel data is extracted, and the QR code algorithm is applied locally to recover the encoded text, URL, or data.
howToUse:
How to Use QR Code Decoder

Step 1: Click the upload area or drag a QR code image file into the input zone.

Step 2: The tool processes the image and attempts to decode the QR code.

Step 3: The decoded text or URL appears in the output area.

Step 4: If the QR code cannot be decoded, the tool reports the error — try uploading a clearer or higher-resolution image.
whyUse:
Why Use QR Code Decoder

You encounter QR codes in the wild — on receipts, business cards, marketing materials — and need to extract the encoded data without scanning with your phone camera. Perhaps you want to verify what URL a QR code points to before scanning it (a security practice against QR code phishing), or you need to extract data from a QR code image you've received. The decoder handles this without any external API calls.

faq.question: What image formats are supported?
faq.answer: The tool accepts PNG, JPEG, GIF, and BMP image files. These are the standard formats that browsers can process via the Canvas API. SVG and WebP may also work depending on browser support.

faq.question: What if the QR code is low resolution?
faq.answer: The decoder works best with QR codes that are at least 200×200 pixels. Very small or blurry images may fail to decode. Try resizing the image to at least 300×300 pixels before uploading.

faq.question: Can it decode multiple QR codes in one image?
faq.answer: The tool processes the first QR code it detects in the image. For images containing multiple QR codes, you may need to crop to the specific code you want to decode.

faq.question: Does this work with QR codes containing Chinese/Japanese characters?
faq.answer: Yes. QR codes can encode UTF-8 text in byte mode. The decoder handles multi-byte Unicode characters, including CJK characters, emoji, and other non-ASCII text.

title: Barcode Generator
whatIs:
What is Barcode Generator

The Barcode Generator creates one-dimensional barcodes from numeric or alphanumeric input using canvas-based rendering. It supports multiple barcode formats including Code 128 (full ASCII), Code 39 (uppercase alphanumeric), EAN-13 (retail products), UPC-A (US retail), and Interleaved 2 of 5 (numeric pairs). Each format follows its respective industry standard, including proper quiet zones (whitespace margins), checksum calculation, and human-readable text below the barcode.
howToUse:
How to Use Barcode Generator

Step 1: Enter the data to encode in the input area.

Step 2: Select the barcode format from the options (Code 128, Code 39, EAN-13, UPC-A, ITF).

Step 3: Click Transform. The tool renders a barcode image on the canvas.

Step 4: The generated barcode appears in the output area with the encoded text below it. Save as PNG for printing.
whyUse:
Why Use Barcode Generator

Barcodes are essential for inventory management, product labeling, asset tracking, and event ticketing. While QR codes store more data, traditional barcodes remain the standard in retail (EAN-13/UPC-A) and logistics (Code 128). Generating barcodes client-side is useful for prototyping label designs, testing point-of-sale systems, and creating barcodes for internal tracking without needing a dedicated barcode printer or subscription service.

faq.question: Which barcode format should I use?
faq.answer: Use Code 128 for general-purpose barcodes — it supports all 128 ASCII characters and is the most widely used format. Use EAN-13 for European retail products (13-digit), UPC-A for US retail (12-digit), Code 39 for alphanumeric industrial codes, and ITF for shipping carton markings.

faq.question: What is a quiet zone?
faq.answer: The quiet zone is the mandatory whitespace margin around the barcode that scanners need to detect the barcode's edges. The generator includes the correct quiet zone width for each format — Code 128 needs 10 modules, EAN-13 needs 11 modules on the left and 7 on the right.

faq.question: Does the generator calculate checksums automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. For formats that require checksums (EAN-13, UPC-A, Code 128), the generator computes and appends the check digit automatically. You don't need to include it in your input.

faq.question: Can these barcodes be scanned by phone cameras?
faq.answer: Yes. Standard barcode formats like Code 128, EAN-13, and UPC-A are recognized by all modern smartphone camera apps and barcode scanner applications.

title: Barcode Decoder
whatIs:
What is Barcode Decoder

The Barcode Decoder reads and extracts the encoded data from one-dimensional barcode images. It processes uploaded images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP) using canvas-based pixel analysis to detect barcode patterns and decode the underlying data. The decoder supports the same formats as the Barcode Generator: Code 128, Code 39, EAN-13, UPC-A, and Interleaved 2 of 5.
howToUse:
How to Use Barcode Decoder

Step 1: Upload a barcode image by clicking the upload area or dragging a file into it.

Step 2: The tool processes the image and identifies the barcode pattern.

Step 3: The decoded data appears in the output area, along with the detected barcode format.

Step 4: If decoding fails, try uploading a higher-resolution or clearer image with good contrast.
whyUse:
Why Use Barcode Decoder

When you receive a barcode image — from a product photo, a scanned document, or a screenshot — you need to extract the encoded data without a physical scanner. This is useful for verifying product barcodes, reading UPC codes from product images for price comparison, and extracting tracking numbers from shipping labels. The client-side decoder means you can process barcode images without uploading them to a third-party service, which matters when the barcode encodes sensitive information.

faq.question: What makes a good barcode image for decoding?
faq.answer: The barcode should be in focus, well-lit, with high contrast between the bars and background. The image should be at least 300 pixels wide for reliable decoding. Avoid images with shadows, glare, or perspective distortion.

faq.question: Can it read barcodes from angled photos?
faq.answer: The decoder works best with straight-on images. Mild angles (up to about 15 degrees) are usually handled, but steep angles or curved surfaces (like barcodes on bottles) may cause decoding failures.

faq.question: Does it verify the checksum?
faq.answer: The decoder reads the barcode data and, for formats with checksums (EAN-13, UPC-A), verifies the check digit. If the checksum doesn't match, the decoder reports an error.

faq.question: Can it decode Data Matrix or PDF417 barcodes?
faq.answer: This tool focuses on one-dimensional (linear) barcodes. Two-dimensional formats like Data Matrix, PDF417, and Aztec codes require different decoding algorithms and are not currently supported.

title: Passphrase Generator
whatIs:
What is Passphrase Generator

The Passphrase Generator creates memorable passphrases by randomly selecting words from a curated 256-word dictionary (based on the PGP word list) and joining them with a configurable separator. You can choose 3–10 words and a custom separator (dash, space, dot, etc.). Each word is selected using crypto.getRandomValues() for cryptographic randomness, producing passphrases with entropy ranging from 36 bits (3 words) to 120 bits (10 words).
howToUse:
How to Use Passphrase Generator

Step 1: Set the Words count — 5 words (60 bits) is a good default for most use cases.

Step 2: Choose a separator character — dash (-) is the most common for passphrases, but you can use space, dot, underscore, or any single character.

Step 3: Click Generate. A new random passphrase appears in the output.

Step 4: Click Generate again for a different passphrase until you find one you like.
whyUse:
Why Use Passphrase Generator

Passphrases are easier to remember and type than random character strings while providing equal or greater entropy. A 5-word passphrase like tiger-rocket-ocean-purple-frozen is more memorable than kR7$mP2xQ9vN but has more entropy (60 bits vs ~53 bits). Passphrases are recommended by NIST, used by password managers (Diceware), and are the standard approach for master password generation. The 256-word list ensures each word is short (3-6 letters) and distinctive.

faq.question: How many words should I use?
faq.answer: 5 words provides 60 bits of entropy, suitable for most passwords. 6 words (72 bits) for important accounts. 7+ words for master passwords or encryption keys. The generator shows the entropy alongside the output.

faq.question: Why only 256 words instead of the full English dictionary?
faq.answer: The 256-word list (2^8 words) means each word contributes exactly 8 bits of entropy, making entropy calculation trivial. These words are also selected to be short, distinct, and unambiguous — you won't confuse 'flame' with 'flames' or 'there' with 'their'.

faq.question: Can I use this for BIP-39 seed phrases?
faq.answer: No. BIP-39 uses a specific 2048-word list defined in the Bitcoin Improvement Proposal. This tool uses a different word list. For BIP-39 seed phrases, use a dedicated BIP-39 generator.

faq.question: Is a passphrase more secure than a random password?
faq.answer: For the same entropy level, yes — not because the passphrase is inherently more secure, but because users are more likely to remember and correctly type a passphrase, reducing the temptation to write it down or reuse it.

title: Password Entropy Calculator
whatIs:
What is Password Entropy Calculator

The Password Entropy Calculator measures the information entropy of a password in bits. It determines the character pool size by detecting which character classes are present (lowercase, uppercase, digits, symbols) and calculates entropy as length × log₂(pool_size). This gives you a quantitative measure of how resistant the password is to brute-force attacks, independent of the specific characters used.
howToUse:
How to Use Password Entropy Calculator

Step 1: Enter a password in the input area.

Step 2: Click Transform. The tool analyzes the character classes present.

Step 3: Review the output — it shows the password length, the character pool size (how many possible characters each position could be), and the total entropy in bits.

Step 4: Use the entropy value to assess security: 60+ bits is fair, 80+ bits is strong, 120+ bits is excellent.
whyUse:
Why Use Password Entropy Calculator

Password strength meters in browsers and apps use subjective labels (weak, medium, strong) that don't tell you the actual security level. Entropy in bits provides an objective, comparable metric. Knowing your password's entropy helps you make informed decisions — if your master password has 50 bits of entropy, you know it's vulnerable to targeted attacks, regardless of how 'complex' it looks.

faq.question: What entropy level should I aim for?
faq.answer: 60 bits is the minimum for online accounts (10^18 guesses at 10 billion/sec = ~5 years). 80 bits for important accounts. 128+ bits for master passwords and encryption keys, where offline attacks are the threat model.

faq.question: Why doesn't this tool check for dictionary words?
faq.answer: Entropy calculation measures the size of the search space, not whether a specific password appears in a dictionary. A dictionary attack reduces the effective entropy dramatically. Use the Password Pattern Analyzer and Common Password Checker tools alongside this one for a complete picture.

faq.question: How does character pool size affect entropy?
faq.answer: Each additional bit of entropy doubles the number of guesses needed. A 12-character password with a 94-character pool has 79 bits of entropy, while the same length with only lowercase letters (26-char pool) has 56 bits — a difference of 23 bits, or about 8 million times easier to crack.

faq.question: Is entropy the same as security?
faq.answer: No. Entropy measures resistance to brute-force guessing. A password with high entropy but reused across multiple sites is still insecure. Entropy also doesn't account for targeted attacks using personal information (birthdays, pet names) or keyloggers.

title: Password Pattern Analyzer
whatIs:
What is Password Pattern Analyzer

The Password Pattern Analyzer scans a password for common structural weaknesses and insecure patterns. It checks for repeated characters (three or more identical characters in a row), common sequences (123, abc, qwerty, password), insufficient length (under 10 characters), missing character classes (no uppercase, no digits, no symbols), and other predictable patterns that reduce a password's effective security regardless of its theoretical entropy.
howToUse:
How to Use Password Pattern Analyzer

Step 1: Enter a password in the input area.

Step 2: Click Transform. The tool scans the password for known patterns.

Step 3: Review the list of detected issues — each one identifies a specific weakness (e.g., 'Repeated characters (3+)', 'Common sequence detected').

Step 4: If no issues are found, the tool reports 'No common patterns detected' — but combine this with entropy calculation for a complete assessment.
whyUse:
Why Use Password Pattern Analyzer

Entropy calculation assumes all character positions are equally random, but real passwords often have predictable patterns. A password like Passw0rd! has decent entropy on paper (7.1 bits/char across 94 characters) but is a known breached password with an obvious structure. The pattern analyzer catches these structural weaknesses that pure entropy measurement misses, giving you a more realistic security assessment.

faq.question: Why check for patterns if the password is random?
faq.answer: If your password is truly random (generated by a password manager or random generator), it won't have patterns. The tool is most valuable for passwords you've created manually, where human bias toward patterns inevitably creeps in.

faq.question: What counts as a 'common sequence'?
faq.answer: The tool detects sequential digits (012, 123, 234, ..., 789), sequential letters (abc, qwe, asd), and known weak passwords (password, starwars, letmein). These patterns are the first things automated crackers try.

faq.question: Does this check against breached password databases?
faq.answer: No. The tool checks for structural patterns only, not whether the password appears in known breach databases. For breach checking, use the Common Password Checker tool, which includes a built-in list of the most commonly breached passwords.

faq.question: My password has no patterns but is only 8 characters. Is that enough?
faq.answer: The tool flags lengths under 10 characters because even pattern-free passwords of this length have limited entropy (about 52 bits for a fully random 8-character password with mixed case, digits, and symbols). For important accounts, aim for 12+ characters.

title: Common Password Checker
whatIs:
What is Common Password Checker

The Common Password Checker checks whether a password appears in a built-in list of the most commonly used and breached passwords worldwide. The list includes entries from the RockYou breach analysis, NIST guidelines, and other sources — covering passwords like '123456', 'password', 'qwerty', 'letmein', 'admin', and hundreds of others that appear in the top breached password lists. The check is performed entirely client-side against the embedded list.
howToUse:
How to Use Common Password Checker

Step 1: Enter a password in the input area.

Step 2: Click Transform. The tool checks the password against its built-in common password database.

Step 3: If the password is found, the tool warns you it appears in common password lists.

Step 4: If not found, it confirms the password is not in the built-in list — but this doesn't mean it's secure, just not in the most common ones.
whyUse:
Why Use Common Password Checker

Before adopting a new password, checking it against common password lists is the single most impactful security step. Password crackers try common passwords first — often succeeding within seconds. This tool catches passwords that users believe are unique but are actually among the millions that appear in every breach database. It's the first line of defense before more sophisticated analysis like entropy calculation or pattern detection.

faq.question: How many passwords are in the built-in list?
faq.answer: The list contains the top 30 most commonly breached passwords from the RockYou breach analysis and NIST guidelines. This is a curated subset — for comprehensive breach checking, services like HaveIBeenPwned offer API-based lookups.

faq.question: My password isn't in the list. Is it safe?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. The tool only checks against the most common passwords. A password not in this list could still be weak (low entropy, predictable patterns) or appear in a different breach database. Always combine this with the Password Entropy Calculator and Pattern Analyzer.

faq.question: Does the check happen in the browser?
faq.answer: Yes. The common password list is embedded in the tool's JavaScript code. No password data is sent to any server. The comparison is a simple exact-match lookup against the list.

faq.question: Why is 'password123' not flagged as common?
faq.answer: The tool checks exact matches only. 'password123' is not in the top-30 list (which contains 'password' and '123456' separately). However, 'password123' would be found in more comprehensive breach databases.

title: Password Length Estimator
whatIs:
What is Password Length Estimator

The Password Length Estimator calculates the estimated time to brute-force a password of a given length and character pool size, assuming a cracking speed of 10 billion guesses per second (typical for modern GPU clusters). It computes the total combinations as pool^length and divides by the guessing rate to produce a human-readable crack time. This helps you understand how password length and complexity translate to actual security.
howToUse:
How to Use Password Length Estimator

Step 1: Set the Length — the password length you want to evaluate (4–32 characters).

Step 2: Set the Pool — the character pool size. Common values: 26 (lowercase only), 62 (mixed case + digits), 94 (all printable ASCII).

Step 3: Click Transform. The tool computes the total combinations and estimated crack time.

Step 4: Review the output — it shows the formula (pool^length) and the human-readable crack time at 10B guesses/sec.
whyUse:
Why Use Password Length Estimator

Understanding the relationship between password length, character pool, and crack time helps you make informed decisions about password policies. A 10-character password with 94 characters seems strong but takes only ~2 hours at 10B guesses/sec. Adding just 2 more characters pushes it to ~16,000 years. This tool makes these tradeoffs concrete, which is valuable for security training, policy development, and personal password planning.

faq.question: Why use 10 billion guesses/sec as the baseline?
faq.answer: Modern GPU clusters (8× NVIDIA RTX 4090) can hash approximately 10 billion MD5 hashes per second, 1 billion SHA-256 hashes per second, and hundreds of millions of bcrypt hashes per second. Using 10B/sec is a realistic upper bound for fast hash algorithms.

faq.question: Is this calculation accurate for bcrypt?
faq.answer: The 10B/sec figure applies to fast hashes like MD5 and SHA-256. Bcrypt at 10 rounds is approximately 30,000/sec on the same hardware — about 300,000× slower. Always use a slow hash (bcrypt, Argon2) for password storage.

faq.question: What character pool does a typical password use?
faq.answer: Lowercase only: 26. Lowercase + digits: 36. Mixed case + digits: 62. Full printable ASCII: 94. If the password includes symbols, use 94. For most password policies requiring mixed case + digits, use 62.

faq.question: Does this account for dictionary attacks?
faq.answer: No. This calculates brute-force time (trying every combination). Dictionary attacks, rainbow tables, and pattern-based attacks are dramatically faster for passwords with predictable structures. This tool shows the theoretical maximum security for a truly random password of the given length and pool.

title: PIN Generator
whatIs:
What is PIN Generator

The PIN Generator creates cryptographically secure numeric PIN codes of configurable length (3–12 digits). Each digit is generated independently using crypto.getRandomValues(), ensuring uniform distribution and resistance to prediction. Unlike Math.random(), which uses a deterministic pseudo-random number generator, the Web Crypto API provides true randomness from the operating system's entropy pool.
howToUse:
How to Use PIN Generator

Step 1: Set the Length — 6 digits is the default for most PINs (ATM cards, phone locks). 4 digits for simpler applications.

Step 2: Click Generate. A random PIN appears in the output.

Step 3: Click Generate again for a new PIN. Each click produces a completely independent random PIN.
whyUse:
Why Use PIN Generator

PINs are used everywhere: ATM cards, phone locks, two-factor authentication, smart locks, and parental controls. A 6-digit PIN has only 1 million possible combinations, making cryptographic randomness essential — a predictable PIN generator (like one seeded from the current time) would make PINs guessable. This tool ensures each digit is truly random, giving the PIN the maximum possible security for its length.

faq.question: How secure is a 4-digit PIN?
faq.answer: A 4-digit PIN has 10,000 possible combinations. At 1 guess per second (the typical lockout rate), it takes up to ~3 hours to try all combinations. At 100 guesses/sec (no lockout), it takes less than 2 minutes. 4-digit PINs are only appropriate when combined with lockout mechanisms.

faq.question: How secure is a 6-digit PIN?
faq.answer: A 6-digit PIN has 1,000,000 combinations. With a 3-attempt lockout, it's resistant to brute-force. Without lockout, 100 guesses/sec takes ~3 hours. For high-security applications, use 8+ digits or switch to alphanumeric passwords.

faq.question: Why can't I just use Math.random() for PINs?
faq.answer: Math.random() is a pseudo-random number generator that produces predictable sequences if the seed is known (often derived from the system clock). An attacker who knows the approximate time a PIN was generated could narrow the possibilities. crypto.getRandomValues() uses the OS entropy pool and is cryptographically unpredictable.

faq.question: Can I generate PINs for specific formats (e.g., no leading zero)?
faq.answer: The tool generates PINs with any leading digit, including zero. If your system doesn't accept leading zeros, simply regenerate until you get a PIN without one, or use the Random Password Generator with digits-only alphabet.

title: Memorable Password Generator
whatIs:
What is Memorable Password Generator

The Memorable Password Generator creates passwords that balance memorability with security by combining real English words with numbers and symbols. It selects two random words from a 256-word dictionary, capitalizes the first letter of the first word, and appends a random two-digit number and a random symbol. The result looks like Tiger-moon42! — memorable enough to recall after seeing it once, but with sufficient complexity for most authentication systems.
howToUse:
How to Use Memorable Password Generator

Step 1: Click Generate. A memorable password appears in the output.

Step 2: Click Generate again for a different password until you find one you like.

Step 3: Copy the password and use it immediately — don't save it in a text file.
whyUse:
Why Use Memorable Password Generator

Many password policies require uppercase, lowercase, digits, and symbols — but purely random strings meeting these requirements are hard to remember. The memorable password format gives you the best of both worlds: a password that passes strength requirements while being easy to recall. The Word-word00! pattern is used by many password managers as their default generation format because it scores well in both security and usability.

faq.question: How many possible combinations does this generator have?
faq.answer: With a 256-word dictionary, 2 words, 100 numbers, and 7 symbols: 256 × 256 × 100 × 7 = 45,875,200 combinations (~25.4 bits of entropy). This is adequate for low-to-medium security use cases but not for master passwords.

faq.question: Is this more secure than a random character password?
faq.answer: For the same length, a random character password has more entropy because each position has more possible values. The memorable password trades entropy for memorability. For high-security use cases, the Random Password Generator is better.

faq.question: Why are the words capitalized this way?
faq.answer: The first letter of the first word is capitalized (Tiger), while the second word stays lowercase (moon). This meets 'uppercase letter' requirements without making the entire password hard to read.

faq.question: Can I customize the format?
faq.answer: The generator uses a fixed format optimized for the most common password policies. For custom formats, use the Passphrase Generator (configurable separator and word count) or the Random Password Generator (configurable character sets and length).

title: Password Comparison Tool
whatIs:
What is Password Comparison Tool

The Password Comparison Tool performs a direct string comparison between two passwords to check if they're identical. It compares the two inputs character by character and reports whether they match or differ. This is useful for verifying that a password you've typed twice (e.g., in a 'Create Password' and 'Confirm Password' form) actually matches, or for comparing a password against a known hash or reference string.
howToUse:
How to Use Password Comparison Tool

Step 1: Enter the first password in the left input area (Input).

Step 2: Enter the second password in the right input area (Second Input).

Step 3: Click Transform. The tool compares the two strings.

Step 4: The output shows ✓ Identical or ✗ Different.
whyUse:
Why Use Password Comparison Tool

When testing password forms, verifying password reset flows, or comparing password entries across systems, you need a quick way to confirm two strings match. While this could be done with any text editor, the dedicated tool provides a clear, unambiguous answer and runs entirely in your browser — the passwords are never transmitted anywhere.

faq.question: Does this compare password hashes?
faq.answer: No. This tool compares the raw text strings. If you need to compare password hashes, use the Hash Comparison Tool instead.

faq.question: Is the comparison case-sensitive?
faq.answer: Yes. 'Password' and 'password' would be reported as different. The comparison is an exact string match, character by character.

faq.question: Can I use this to compare encrypted values?
faq.answer: No. This tool does raw string comparison. Encrypted or encoded values (Base64, hex) would need to match exactly, including any padding characters.

faq.question: Does this store the passwords anywhere?
faq.answer: No. The comparison happens in memory within the browser's JavaScript runtime. Nothing is saved to disk, local storage, or transmitted to any server.
